name: Narrative analysis
summary: Stories are treated as stories: divide each account into narrative segments, code their structure (after Labov and Waletzky), read for themes, and write a storyline for each case.

seed_codes.name: Abstract
seed_codes.definition: A summary of what the story is about, often at the start.

seed_codes.name: Orientation
seed_codes.definition: Who, when, where, and in what situation.

seed_codes.name: Complicating action
seed_codes.definition: What happened: the sequence of events that moves the story forward.

seed_codes.name: Evaluation
seed_codes.definition: Why the story is worth telling: the teller's stance on what happened.

seed_codes.name: Coda
seed_codes.definition: A closing that brings the story back to the present.

notes: The six structural codes above are added when you choose this method.
Not yet built for this method: the timeline view for each case. The phases, prompts, and structural codes work now.

phases.title: Segmentation
phases.goal: Decide where each story begins and ends within the accounts.
memo_prompts: What marks the edges of a story here: a change of time, place, or speaker?
exit_checklist: Marked the stories in each account
Memoed any stretch that was hard to divide

phases.title: Structural coding
phases.goal: Code the parts of each story with the structural codes.
memo_prompts: Where is the evaluation? What does it tell you about why this was told?
exit_checklist: Checked stories that seem to lack a part

phases.title: Thematic reading
phases.goal: Read the stories for what they are about, as well as how they are built.
memo_prompts: What do the stories do for the people who tell them?
exit_checklist: Coded the themes of each story

phases.title: Storyline per case
phases.goal: Write the storyline of each case in order, from the stories you found.
memo_prompts: How does this person's story move from beginning to end?
exit_checklist: Wrote a storyline for every case
